formulas.name: Single Payment Present Worth & Future Worth
formulas.eq: P = F(1+i)<sup>-n</sup> = F(P/F, i, n);    F = P(1+i)<sup>n</sup> = P(F/P, i, n)
formulas.alt: Compound Amount Factor (F/P, i, n) = (1+i)<sup>n</sup>; Present Worth Factor (P/F, i, n) = (1+i)<sup>-n</sup>
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 1.3: Engineering Economics
formulas.notes: End-of-period compounding convention; i is effective interest rate per period; n is total compounding periods.

formulas.name: Uniform Series Present Worth & Capital Recovery
formulas.eq: (P/A, i, n) = (1+i)n - 1i(1+i)n;    (A/P, i, n) = i(1+i)n(1+i)n - 1
formulas.alt: Capital Recovery annualizes an initial capital expenditure over asset service life n.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 1.3: Engineering Economics
formulas.notes: Used for converting recurring annual O&M expenses into equivalent present worth, and amortizing capital costs.

formulas.name: Uniform Series Future Worth & Sinking Fund
formulas.eq: (F/A, i, n) = (1+i)n - 1i;    (A/F, i, n) = i(1+i)n - 1
formulas.alt: A = F × (A/F, i, n); uniform annual deposit to accumulate future replacement sum F.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 1.3: Engineering Economics
formulas.notes: Used to size municipal reserve sinking funds for storage tank replacement or mechanical equipment rehabilitation.

formulas.name: Capitalized Cost for Perpetual Service Life
formulas.eq: Capitalized Cost = C0 + Ai + ∑ Fk(1+i)k - 1
formulas.alt: As n → ∞, (P/A, i, ∞) = 1i; Present Worth of perpetual annual maintenance is Ai.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 1.3: Engineering Economics
formulas.notes: Applicable to permanent public civil infrastructure: dams, flood channels, aqueducts, and bridges.

formulas.name: Benefit-Cost (B/C) Ratio Analysis
formulas.eq: Conventional B/C = BI(A/P, i, n) + O&M;    Modified B/C = B - O&MI(A/P, i, n)
formulas.alt: Project is economically justified if B/C ≥ 1.0; incremental Δ B / Δ C ≥ 1.0 governs mutually exclusive alternatives.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 1.3: Engineering Economics
formulas.notes: Public agency feasibility standard; B is annual equivalent benefit, I is initial investment, O&M is annual operation/maintenance.

formulas.name: Critical Path Method (CPM) Float & Schedule
formulas.eq: TF = LS - ES = LF - EF;    FF = ES<sub>successor</sub> - EF
formulas.alt: Early Finish EF = ES + Duration; Late Start LS = LF - Duration.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 1.2: Construction Scheduling
formulas.notes: Critical path activities have TF = 0. Delaying critical path activities directly delays project completion.

formulas.name: Soil Phase Relationships (Weight-Volume)
formulas.eq: S · e = w · Gs;    n = e1+e;    gammadry = Gs γw1+e;    gammasat = Gs + e1+e γw
formulas.alt: Submerged/buoyant unit weight γ' = gammasat - γw = Gs - 11+e γw.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 3.1: Geotechnical - Phase Relations
formulas.notes: Fundamental identities linking degree of saturation S, void ratio e, moisture content w, and specific gravity G<sub>s.</sub>

formulas.name: Effective Stress & Critical Seepage Gradient
formulas.eq: σ' = σ - u;    icrit = γ'γw = Gs - 11+e ≈ 1.0
formulas.alt: Piping factor of safety FSpiping = icritiexit = icritΔ h / Δ L.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 3.1 & 4.4: Geotechnical - Effective Stress & Seepage
formulas.notes: When upward seepage gradient i reaches i<sub>crit</sub>, effective vertical stress drops to zero (quicksand/boiling condition).

formulas.name: Rankine Lateral Earth Pressure Coefficients
formulas.eq: Ka = tan2(45° - φ'2) = 1 - sinφ'1 + sinφ';    Kp = tan2(45° + φ'2) = 1 + sinφ'1 - sinφ'
formulas.alt: At-rest coefficient (Jaky): K0 = 1 - sinφ'; Total active thrust Pa = 12 Ka γ H2 acting at H/3 above base.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 3.4: Geotechnical - Retaining Walls
formulas.notes: Active state requires wall outward yield; rigid unyielding basement walls must be designed for higher at-rest pressure K<sub>0.</sub>

formulas.name: Terzaghi Bearing Capacity (Shallow Footings)
formulas.eq: qult = c Nc sc + q Nq + 12 γ B Nγ sγ;    qallow = qultFS
formulas.alt: Square footing shape factors: s<sub>c</sub> = 1.3, s<sub>γ</sub> = 0.8 (factor 0.4); Circular: s<sub>c</sub> = 1.3, s<sub>γ</sub> = 0.6 (factor 0.3).
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 3.3: Geotechnical - Bearing Capacity
formulas.notes: Overburden surcharge q = γ D<sub>f</sub>; water table within depth B below footing base reduces soil unit weight to buoyant γ'.

formulas.name: One-Dimensional Primary Consolidation Settlement
formulas.eq: Sc = Cc H1+e0 log10(σ′0 + Δσ'σ′0)
formulas.alt: Overconsolidated clay with σ′0 + Δσ' > σ′c: Sc = Cr H1+e0 log10(σ′cσ′0) + Cc H1+e0 log10(σ′0 + Δσ'σ′c).
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 3.2: Geotechnical - Settlement
formulas.notes: Evaluate initial effective stress σ′<sub>0</sub> and stress increment Δσ' at mid-depth of the compressible clay stratum.

formulas.name: Rate of Consolidation & Drainage Time
formulas.eq: t = Tv Hdr2cv;    tfield = tlab (Tv,fieldTv,lab) (Hdr,fieldHdr,lab)2
formulas.alt: Time factors: T<sub>v</sub>(50%) = 0.197, T<sub>v</sub>(90%) = 0.848; Single drainage H<sub>dr</sub> = H; Double drainage H<sub>dr</sub> = H/2.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 3.2: Geotechnical - Consolidation
formulas.notes: Consolidation time scales with the square of the maximum drainage path length H<sub>dr</sub><sup>2</sup>.

formulas.name: Soil Gradation Coefficients (USCS Classification)
formulas.eq: Cu = D60D10;    Cc = (D30)2D10 D60
formulas.alt: Well-graded gravel (GW): C<sub>u</sub> ≥ 4 and 1 ≤ C<sub>c</sub> ≤ 3; Well-graded sand (SW): C<sub>u</sub> ≥ 6 and 1 ≤ C<sub>c</sub> ≤ 3.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 3.1: Geotechnical - USCS Soil Classification
formulas.notes: Coarse-grained soils have < 50% passing No. 200 sieve; gravel vs sand split on No. 4 sieve (4.75 mm).

formulas.name: Atterberg Limits & Plasticity Chart A-Line
formulas.eq: PI = LL - PL;    PI<sub>A-Line</sub> = 0.73(LL - 20)
formulas.alt: Plots above A-Line are inorganic clays (C); plots below are inorganic silts (M) or organic soils (O); LL ≥ 50 indicates high plasticity (H).
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 3.1: Geotechnical - Atterberg Limits
formulas.notes: Hatched dual classification zone: 4 ≤ PI ≤ 7 with LL between 12 and 29 yields CL-ML.

formulas.name: Concrete Water-Cementitious Ratio & Batch Yield
formulas.eq: w/cm = WwaterWcement + Wpozzolan;    Yield (ft3) = ∑ Wbatchgammaconcrete;    Ry = Yield27.0 ft3
formulas.alt: Relative yield R<sub>y</sub> > 1.00 indicates overyielding (excess batch volume); R<sub>y</sub> < 1.00 indicates underyielding.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 1.5: Materials - Concrete Mix Design
formulas.notes: Standard unit weight of normal concrete γ ≈ 145 - 150 lb/ft<sup>3</sup>; w/cm strictly governs 28-day compressive strength f′<sub>c.</sub>

formulas.name: Thermoplastic Pipe Dimension Ratio (DR) & Pressure Class
formulas.eq: DR = Dot;    Pressure Rating (PR) = 2 · HDSDR - 1 = 2 · HDS(Do / t) - 1
formulas.alt: Barlow's hoop stress: σ = P(Do - t)2t; Hydrostatic Design Stress HDS = HDB × Design Factor.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.1: Closed Conduit - Piping Materials
formulas.notes: Lower DR designates thicker wall and higher internal pressure capability (e.g. DR 14 PVC = 305 ψ; DR 18 = 235 ψ).

formulas.name: Reinforced Concrete Pipe (RCP) D-Load Rating
formulas.eq: Three-Edge Bearing Load (lb/linear ft) = D-Load × D<sub>inside</sub> (ft)
formulas.alt: Bedding factor Bf: Required pipe laboratory TEB = WtrenchBf; Class B bedding Bf = 1.9.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 1.5: Materials - Concrete Pipe
formulas.notes: ASTM C76 defines pipe classes by 0.01-inch crack D-load (Class III = 1,350 lb/ft/ft, Class IV = 2,000 lb/ft/ft, Class V = 3,000 lb/ft/ft).

formulas.name: Aggregate Fineness Modulus (ASTM C33)
formulas.eq: FM = ∑ Cumulative % Retained on Sieves No. 4, 8, 16, 30, 50, 100100
formulas.alt: ASTM C33 specification for concrete sand requires 2.3 ≤ FM ≤ 3.1.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 1.5: Materials - Aggregates
formulas.notes: Do not include the No. 200 sieve or pan in the Fineness Modulus calculation; higher FM denotes coarser sand.

formulas.name: Fluid Junction Mass Balance & Complete Mixing
formulas.eq: Qdown Cdown = ∑ Qi Ci ⇒ Cdown = Qstream Cstream + Qeff CeffQstream + Qeff
formulas.alt: Steady-state conservative constituent balance across fluid mixing nodes; total mass flux is conserved.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.5: Environmental - Complete Mixing
formulas.notes: Total downstream discharge Q<sub>down</sub> = Q<sub>stream</sub> + Q<sub>eff</sub>; forgetting to add effluent discharge causes major error.

formulas.name: Clarifier Hydraulic Surface Overflow Rate (SOR)
formulas.eq: SOR = QAplan = Qπ D24 [gpd/ft2]
formulas.alt: Particles with settling velocity v<sub>s</sub> ≥ SOR achieve 100% capture; side water depth governs detention time, not SOR.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.6: Wastewater - Primary Clarifiers
formulas.notes: Typical primary clarifier design values: SOR = 800 - 1,200 gpd/ft<sup>2</sup>; secondary clarifiers: 400 - 800 gpd/ft<sup>2</sup>.

formulas.name: Secondary Clarifier Solids Loading Rate (SLR)
formulas.eq: SLR = Applied Solids (lb/day)Aplan = (Q + Qr) × MLSS × 8.34Aplan [lb/day/ft2]
formulas.alt: State point underflow concentration: Cu = Q + QrQr MLSS = 1+rr MLSS, where r = Qr / Q.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.6: Wastewater - Secondary Clarifiers
formulas.notes: Applied solids to secondary clarifiers MUST include both forward plant flow Q and return activated sludge recycle flow Q<sub>r.</sub>

formulas.name: Triangular 90° V-Notch Weir Flow Measurement
formulas.eq: Q = 2.50 H<sup>2.5</sup> (USCS: Q in cfs, H in feet) | Q = 1.38 H<sup>2.5</sup> (SI: Q in m<sup>3</sup>/s, H in meters)
formulas.alt: General angle θ: Q = 815 Cd √2g tan(θ2) H2.5.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.2: Open Channel - Weirs
formulas.notes: V-notch weirs maintain high flow measurement precision across a wide dynamic discharge range due to proportional contraction.

formulas.name: Rectangular Suppressed & Contracted Weirs (Francis)
formulas.eq: Q = 3.33 (L - 0.1 n H) H<sup>1.5</sup> (USCS units: Q in cfs, L, H in ft)
formulas.alt: Suppressed weir (n = 0, no end contractions): Q = 3.33 L H<sup>1.5</sup>; Two end contractions (n = 2): Q = 3.33 (L - 0.2H) H<sup>1.5</sup>.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.2: Open Channel - Weirs
formulas.notes: Head H must be measured at least 4H upstream of the weir crest to avoid the water surface drawdown curve.

formulas.name: Flocculation Velocity Gradient (G) & Camp Number
formulas.eq: G = √Pμ V;    Camp-Stein Dimensionless Number = G · t = G (VQ)
formulas.alt: P = 550 × HP in USCS (	ext{ft} · lb/s); Camp number G · t represents total particle collision opportunity.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.6: Water Treatment - Flocculation
formulas.notes: Typical water treatment targets: G = 20 - 70 s<sup>-1</sup>; Camp number G · t = 10<sup>4</sup> - 10<sup>5</sup>; excessive G shears floc.

formulas.name: Darcy-Weisbach Energy Loss Equation
formulas.eq: hf = f (LD) V22g = 8 f Lπ2 g D5 Q2;    hm = ∑ K V22g
formulas.alt: Total head loss hL = hf + hm; Laminar regime (Re < 2,000): f = 64Re.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.1: Closed Conduit - Friction Loss
formulas.notes: Universal theoretical equation for any Newtonian fluid; valid for laminar, transitional, and turbulent flow regimes.

formulas.name: Swamee-Jain Explicit Friction Factor Equation
formulas.eq: f = 0.25[log10(ε3.7D + 5.74Re0.9)]2
formulas.alt: Explicit approximation of the implicit Colebrook equation; agrees within 1% over 5,000 ≤ Re ≤ 10<sup>8</sup> and 10<sup>-6</sup> ≤ ε/D ≤ 10<sup>-2</sup>.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.1: Closed Conduit - Darcy-Weisbach
formulas.notes: Ensure common logarithm (log<sub>10</sub>) is used, NOT natural log (ln); eliminate iterative Moody diagram hunting.

formulas.name: Hazen-Williams Pipe Friction Loss (USCS units)
formulas.eq: hf = 10.44 L Q1.852C1.852 d4.87 [Q in gpm, d in inches, L in ft];    hf = 4.73 L Q1.852C1.852 D4.87 [Q in cfs, D in ft]
formulas.alt: Flow velocity: V = 1.318 C R<sub>h</sub><sup>0.63</sup> S<sup>0.54</sup> (ft/s units); C = 140 - 150 for PVC/HDPE; C = 100 for older unlined cast iron.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.1: Closed Conduit - Hazen-Williams
formulas.notes: Empirical formula applicable strictly to water flow at normal ambient temperatures (60°F); lower C means rougher pipe.

formulas.name: Total Dynamic Head & Pump Power
formulas.eq: TDH = hstatic + hf + hm;    WHP = Q · TDH · SG3,960;    Motor HP = WHPetapump etamotor
formulas.alt: Brake Horsepower BHP = WHPetapump; Combined wire-to-water efficiency etatotal = etapump × etamotor.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.1: Closed Conduit - Pumps
formulas.notes: Q in gpm, TDH in ft; 3,960 conversion constant arises from (33,000 ft · lb/min/hp) / 8.34 lb/gal.

formulas.name: Pump Affinity Laws (Speed & Diameter Scaling)
formulas.eq: Q2Q1 = N2N1 (D2D1);    H2H1 = (N2N1)2 (D2D1)2;    P2P1 = (N2N1)3 (D2D1)3
formulas.alt: Impeller trim at constant rpm: Q ∝ D, H ∝ D<sup>2</sup>, BHP ∝ D<sup>3</sup>; VFD speed control at constant diameter: Q ∝ N, H ∝ N<sup>2</sup>, BHP ∝ N<sup>3</sup>.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.1: Closed Conduit - Affinity Laws
formulas.notes: Power scales with the CUBE of speed or diameter; small changes in impeller diameter or speed dramatically shift power demand.

formulas.name: Net Positive Suction Head Available (NPSHa)
formulas.eq: NPSHa = Patmγ ± zs - hfs - Pvpγ
formulas.alt: Cavitation occurs when NPSHa < NPSHr; Thoma cavitation parameter σ = NPSHrHtotal.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.1: Closed Conduit - Pumps
formulas.notes: Suction lift: static head z<sub>s</sub> is subtracted when reservoir water surface is BELOW pump centerline; added for flooded suction.

formulas.name: Joukowsky Water Hammer Pressure Surge
formulas.eq: Δ H = a Δ Vg;    Δ P = γ Δ H144 = ρ a Δ V144;    tc = 2La
formulas.alt: Wave speed: a = √K/ρ1 + (K/E)(D/t); rapid valve closure occurs when closing time t ≤ tc = 2L/a.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.1: Closed Conduit - Water Hammer
formulas.notes: Rapid valve closure halts fluid momentum, generating maximum acoustic pressure rise; slow closure (t > 2L/a) reduces surge.

formulas.name: Manning's Equation for Uniform Gravity Flow
formulas.eq: Q = 1.486n A Rh2/3 S01/2 (USCS) | Q = 1.0n A Rh2/3 S01/2 (SI)
formulas.alt: Hydraulic radius Rh = A / P; Trapezoid area A = (b + zy)y; Wetted perimeter P = b + 2y√1+z2.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.2: Open Channel Hydraulics
formulas.notes: In USCS units, the 1.486 conversion factor (1.4859 = 1 m<sup>1/3</sup>/ft<sup>1/3</sup>) is mandatory; for full circular pipe R<sub>h</sub> = D/4.

formulas.name: Critical Depth & Minimum Specific Energy (Rectangular)
formulas.eq: yc = (q2g)1/3 = [(Q/b)2g]1/3;    Emin = 1.5 yc
formulas.alt: Froude number Fr = V√g Dh; Fr < 1 Subcritical (tranquil); Fr = 1 Critical; Fr > 1 Supercritical (rapid).
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.2: Open Channel - Critical Flow
formulas.notes: The minimum specific energy relation E<sub>min</sub> = 1.5 y<sub>c</sub> is strictly valid ONLY for rectangular cross sections.

formulas.name: General Critical Flow Criterion (Non-Rectangular Sections)
formulas.eq: Q2 Tg A3 = 1 ⇒ V22g = Dh2
formulas.alt: Hydraulic depth Dh = A / T, where T is top water surface width; Triangular channel (zH:1V): yc = (2Q2g z2)1/5.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.2: Open Channel - Critical Flow
formulas.notes: Governing condition for critical flow in trapezoidal, triangular, circular, or irregular natural river channels.

formulas.name: Hydraulic Jump Sequent Depths & Energy Dissipation
formulas.eq: y2y1 = 12 [√1 + 8 Fr12 - 1];    Δ E = (y2 - y1)34 y1 y2
formulas.alt: Specific force is conserved (M<sub>1</sub> = M<sub>2</sub>); Jump length on horizontal apron: L<sub>j</sub> ≈ 6 y<sub>2</sub> for Fr<sub>1</sub> = 4.5 - 9.0.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.2: Open Channel - Hydraulic Jump
formulas.notes: Hydraulic jump transitions abruptly from supercritical (Fr<sub>1</sub> > 1) to subcritical (Fr<sub>2</sub> < 1); Sequent depths have unequal energies.

formulas.name: Circular Conduit Partial Flow Elements (Manning)
formulas.eq: dD = 0.50 ⇒ Rh = D4,    A = 0.5 Afull
formulas.alt: Maximum discharge occurs at d/D ≈ 0.938 (Q = 1.075 Q<sub>full</sub>); Maximum velocity occurs at d/D ≈ 0.81 (V = 1.14 V<sub>full</sub>).
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.2: Open Channel - Circular Sections
formulas.notes: A pipe flowing full carries LESS flow than a pipe flowing at 94% depth due to crown friction.

formulas.name: Roadside Gutter Spread (HEC-22 Manning Modified)
formulas.eq: Q = 0.56n Sx1.67 SL0.5 T2.67 ⇒ T = [Q · n0.56 Sx1.67 SL0.5]0.375
formulas.alt: Gutter cross-slope S<sub>x</sub> (ft/ft), longitudinal grade S<sub>L</sub> (ft/ft), spread width T (ft); Curb inlet capture efficiency: E = 1 - (1 - L/L<sub>T</sub>)<sup>1.8</sup>.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.2: Open Channel - Pavement Drainage (HEC-22)
formulas.notes: Cross slope S<sub>x</sub> must be entered in dimensionless ft/ft (2% = 0.02), NOT whole percent; sizes allowable street flooding.

formulas.name: Rational Method Peak Runoff Discharge
formulas.eq: Q<sub>p</sub> = C<sub>f</sub> · C · I · A [cfs ≈ acre-in/hr]
formulas.alt: Composite runoff coefficient: Ccomp = ∑ Ci AiAtotal; Frequency factor Cf = 1.0 ( ≤ 10-yr), 1.1 (25-yr), 1.2 (50-yr), 1.25 (100-yr).
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.3: Hydrology - Rational Method
formulas.notes: Valid for small drainage basins (A ≤ 200 acres); rainfall intensity I is evaluated at storm duration equal to time of concentration t<sub>d</sub> = t<sub>c.</sub>

formulas.name: NRCS (SCS) Runoff Curve Number Equation
formulas.eq: Q = (P - 0.2S)2P + 0.8S;    S = 1,000CN - 10
formulas.alt: Initial abstraction Ia = 0.2S; Runoff occurs only when P > 0.2S; Total runoff volume Vol (ac-ft) = Q (in) × A (acres)12.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.3: Hydrology - SCS Method
formulas.notes: Rainfall P and soil potential maximum retention S are in inches; CN integrates soil group (A, B, C, D), land cover, and moisture.

formulas.name: Time of Concentration (NRCS Sheet Flow & Kirpich)
formulas.eq: Tt,sheet = 0.007(n L)0.8P20.5 S0.4 (hr);    tc,Kirpich = 0.0078 L0.77 S-0.385 (min)
formulas.alt: Total time of concentration: t<sub>c</sub> = T<sub>sheet</sub> + T<sub>shallow concentrated</sub> + T<sub>channel flow</sub>; TR-55 limits sheet flow length L ≤ 100 ft.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.3: Hydrology - Time of Concentration
formulas.notes: In Kirpich formula, L is flow path length in feet, S is channel slope in ft/ft (dimensionless).

formulas.name: NRCS Dimensionless Unit Hydrograph Peak Rate
formulas.eq: Qp = 484 A Qexcesstp;    tp = D2 + 0.6 tc
formulas.alt: Time to peak t<sub>p</sub> in hours, watershed area A in square miles, excess runoff Q<sub>excess</sub> = 1.0 inch; Standard shape factor = 484.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.3: Hydrology - Unit Hydrographs
formulas.notes: Shape factor reduces to 284 in flat coastal plains and increases to 600 in steep mountainous catchments.

formulas.name: Muskingum River Reach Flood Routing
formulas.eq: O<sub>2</sub> = C<sub>0</sub> I<sub>2</sub> + C<sub>1</sub> I<sub>1</sub> + C<sub>2</sub> O<sub>1</sub>;    C<sub>0</sub> + C<sub>1</sub> + C<sub>2</sub> = 1.0
formulas.alt: C0 = Δ t - 2KX2K(1-X) + Δ t; C1 = Δ t + 2KX2K(1-X) + Δ t; C2 = 2K(1-X) - Δ t2K(1-X) + Δ t; routing stability: 2KX < Δ t ≤ K.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.3: Hydrology - Flood Routing
formulas.notes: K is reach travel time (storage parameter), X is wedge weighting factor (0 ≤ X ≤ 0.5; natural streams X ≈ 0.1 - 0.3).

formulas.name: Water Quality Volume (WQv) & Flood Risk Probability
formulas.eq: WQv = P · Rv · A12 (ac-ft);    Rv = 0.05 + 0.009 I;    Risk = 1 - (1 - 1T)n
formulas.alt: Annual exceedance probability p = 1/T; Schueler volumetric runoff coefficient R<sub>v</sub> uses percent site imperviousness I (0 - 100%).
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.3: Hydrology - Stormwater Quality & Frequency
formulas.notes: Risk is the binomial probability of equaling or exceeding the T-year event at least once in an n-year design bond period.

formulas.name: Darcy's Law & Actual Pore Seepage Velocity
formulas.eq: Q = K i A = K (Δ hL) A;    v = K i;    vs = vne = K ine
formulas.alt: Darcy velocity v is apparent superficial discharge velocity; actual advective seepage velocity v<sub>s</sub> through interconnected pores is v/n<sub>e.</sub>
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.4: Groundwater Flow
formulas.notes: Contaminant travel time and tracer velocity must ALWAYS be computed using true seepage velocity v<sub>s</sub>, never Darcy velocity v.

formulas.name: Thiem Equation (Confined Aquifer Steady Radial Flow)
formulas.eq: T = K b = Q ln(r2 / r1)2 π (s1 - s2)
formulas.alt: Drawdown relation: s1 - s2 = Q2 π T ln(r2r1); observation wells at radial distances r1 and r2 with drawdowns s1 and s2.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.4: Groundwater - Well Hydraulics
formulas.notes: Confined aquifer thickness b remains fully saturated and constant; piezometric surface remains above top confining bed.

formulas.name: Dupuit Equation (Unconfined Aquifer Radial Flow)
formulas.eq: K = Q ln(r2 / r1)π (h22 - h12) ⇒ Q = π K (h22 - h12)ln(r2 / r1)
formulas.alt: At well casing (r = rw, h = hw) and outer radius of influence (r = R, h = H0): Q = π K (H02 - hw2)ln(R / rw).
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.4: Groundwater - Unconfined Well Flow
formulas.notes: Unconfined flow involves a sloping phreatic water table where flow area shrinks toward the wellbore; heads are SQUARED.

formulas.name: Theis & Cooper-Jacob Transient Well Equations
formulas.eq: s = Q4 π T W(u);    u = r2 S4 T t;    s = Q4 π T ln(2.25 T tr2 S) [for u < 0.05]
formulas.alt: Cooper-Jacob base-10: s = 2.303 Q4 π T log10(2.25 T tr2 S); Transmissivity T = 2.303 Q4 π Δ s per log cycle.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.4: Groundwater - Transient Well Flow
formulas.notes: Non-equilibrium well equations quantify drawdown cone development over pumping time t in confined aquifers.

formulas.name: 2D Seepage Flow Net & Dam Seepage Rate
formulas.eq: q = K H (NfNd) [ft3/(s · ft)];    Δ h = HNd
formulas.alt: Shape factor = Nf / Nd; Anisotropic hydraulic conductivity transformed coordinate equivalent: K' = √Kh Kv.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.4: Groundwater - Seepage & Flow Nets
formulas.notes: H is the total differential head loss between upstream and downstream pools (H = H<sub>up</sub> - H<sub>down</sub>), not pool elevation.

formulas.name: Ghyben-Herzberg Coastal Saltwater Intrusion
formulas.eq: z = (ρfρs - ρf) hf = (1.0001.025 - 1.000) hf = 40 hf
formulas.alt: Total freshwater thickness above impermeable base = h<sub>f</sub> + z = 41 h<sub>f</sub>; every 1.0 ft of water table decline causes 40 ft of saltwater upconing.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.4: Groundwater - Saltwater Intrusion
formulas.notes: Hydrostatic equilibrium principle between immiscible freshwater and denser seawater (ho<sub>s</sub> = 1.025 g/cm<sup>3</sup>).

formulas.name: Streeter-Phelps Dissolved Oxygen Sag Equation
formulas.eq: D(t) = kd L0kr - kd (e-kd t - e-kr t) + D0 e-kr t;    DO(t) = DOsat - D(t)
formulas.alt: Oxygen deficit D = DO<sub>sat</sub> - DO; k<sub>d</sub> is deoxygenation rate, k<sub>r</sub> is atmospheric reaeration rate (base e, day<sup>-1</sup>).
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.5: Environmental - Oxygen Sag Model
formulas.notes: Balances biochemical deoxygenation against physical surface reaeration in a 1D plug-flow stream receiving organic wastewater effluent.

formulas.name: Critical Travel Time & Minimum River DO Deficit
formulas.eq: tc = 1kr - kd ln[krkd(1 - D0(kr - kd)kd L0)];    Dc = kdkr L0 e-kd tc
formulas.alt: Minimum river dissolved oxygen: DO<sub>min</sub> = DO<sub>sat</sub> - D<sub>c</sub>; distance to critical sag point x<sub>c</sub> = U · t<sub>c.</sub>
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.5: Environmental - Oxygen Sag
formulas.notes: Occurs at the inflection point where reaeration rate exactly balances deoxygenation rate (dD/dt = 0).

formulas.name: Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) Kinetics
formulas.eq: BOD<sub>t</sub> = L<sub>0</sub> (1 - e<sup>-k t</sup>) = BOD<sub>u</sub> (1 - e<sup>-k t</sup>);    k<sub>T</sub> = k<sub>20</sub> (1.047)<sup>T - 20</sup>
formulas.alt: 5-day BOD to ultimate BOD: BODu = BOD51 - e-5k; Reaeration temperature correction: kr,T = kr,20 (1.024)T - 20.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.5: Environmental - BOD Kinetics
formulas.notes: BOD exertion follows 1st-order kinetics; deoxygenation uses θ = 1.047; reaeration gas diffusion uses θ = 1.024.

formulas.name: Nitrogenous Biochemical Oxygen Demand (NBOD)
formulas.eq: NBOD = 4.57 × [NH<sub>3</sub>-N (mg/L)]
formulas.alt: Complete biological nitrification stoichiometry: NH<sub>4</sub><sup>+</sup> + 2O<sub>2</sub> → NO<sub>3</sub><sup>-</sup> + H<sub>2O</sub> + 2H<sup>+</sup>; 64 g O<sub>2</sub> / 14 g N = 4.57.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.5: Environmental - Oxygen Demand
formulas.notes: Nitrification consumes 4.57 mg O<sub>2</sub> per mg of ammonia nitrogen oxidized to nitrate; partial oxidation to nitrite consumes 3.43 mg O<sub>2</sub>.

formulas.name: Solute Sorption Retardation in Groundwater
formulas.eq: Rd = 1 + (ρbn) Kd;    vplume = vsRd
formulas.alt: Organic carbon partitioning: K<sub>d</sub> = f<sub>oc</sub> K<sub>oc</sub>; Bulk dry soil density ρ<sub>b</sub>, total porosity n, distribution coefficient K<sub>d.</sub>
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.5: Environmental - Solute Transport
formulas.notes: Adsorption retards contaminant plume velocity relative to groundwater seepage (R<sub>d</sub> ≥ 1.0); R<sub>d</sub> = 1.0 is an unretarded conservative tracer.

formulas.name: Clean Water Act Section 303(d) TMDL Allocation
formulas.eq: TMDL = ∑ WLA + ∑ LA + MOS
formulas.alt: Waste Load Allocation (WLA) for NPDES point sources; Load Allocation (LA) for nonpoint/background; Margin of Safety (MOS).
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.5: Environmental Regulations
formulas.notes: TMDL sets the maximum allowable daily pollutant assimilative capacity for impaired waterbodies failing water quality criteria.

formulas.name: Disinfection CT Compliance & Log Inactivation
formulas.eq: CT = C × t10 [mg · min/L];    t10 = T × BF = (VQ) × BF
formulas.alt: Chick-Watson 1st-order disinfection kinetics: ln(N/N<sub>0</sub>) = -k C<sup>n</sup> t; 3-log (99.9%) Giardia; 4-log (99.99%) virus inactivation.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.6: Water Treatment - Disinfection
formulas.notes: Mandates effective contact time t<sub>10</sub> (time for 10% of water to pass basin), NOT theoretical detention time T = V/Q.

formulas.name: Alum Coagulation Chemistry & Alkalinity Deficit
formulas.eq: 1.0 mg/L Alum [Al<sub>2</sub>(SO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub> · 14H<sub>2O</sub>] consumes 0.50 mg/L Alkalinity as CaCO<sub>3</sub>
formulas.alt: Mass rate: lb/day = Q(MGD) × Dosage(mg/L) × 8.34; Alum coagulation releases 6 H<sup>+</sup> ions per mole.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.6: Water Treatment - Coagulation
formulas.notes: Sufficient natural alkalinity residual (minimum 20 mg/L as CaCO<sub>3</sub>) is required to prevent pH crash and alum floc destabilization.

formulas.name: Lime-Soda Ash Precipitation Softening Stoichiometry
formulas.eq: TH > TA ⇒ CH = TA,    NCH = TH - TA;    TH ≤ TA ⇒ CH = TH,    NCH = 0
formulas.alt: Lime [Ca(OH)<sub>2</sub>] removes carbonate hardness and CO<sub>2</sub>; Soda ash [Na<sub>2CO,3</sub>] removes non-carbonate hardness (permanent hardness).
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.6: Water Treatment - Softening
formulas.notes: Total Hardness TH = Ca<sup>2+</sup> + Mg<sup>2+</sup>; Total Alkalinity TA = HCO<sub>3</sub><sup>-</sup>; all concentrations expressed in equivalent mg/L as CaCO<sub>3</sub>.

formulas.name: Granular Media Filtration & Backwash Fluidization
formulas.eq: Filtration Rate = QAbed [gpm/ft2];    vmf = g(ρs - ρ) d2150 μ e31 - e
formulas.alt: Bed expansion: LeL = 1 - e1 - ee; Clean bed head loss (Kozeny-Carman): hL = 150 ν (1-e)2g e3 ψ2 (vd2) L.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.6: Water Treatment - Filtration
formulas.notes: Rapid sand filter loading rates: 2 - 6 gpm/ft<sup>2</sup>; Upward backwash fluidization velocity: 12 - 20 gpm/ft<sup>2</sup> to achieve 20 - 30% expansion.

formulas.name: Membrane Separation Recovery & Transmembrane Pressure
formulas.eq: Y = (QpQf) × 100%;    TMP = (Pfeed + Pconc2) - Pperm
formulas.alt: Mass balance: Qf Cf = Qp Cp + Qc Cc; Salt rejection: R = (1 - CpCf) × 100%.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.6: Water Treatment - Membranes
formulas.notes: RO and NF membrane fluxes are driven by net driving pressure (TMP - Δπ, where Δπ is differential osmotic pressure).

formulas.name: Water Distribution Pressure & Storage Tank Sizing
formulas.eq: P<sub>fire</sub> ≥ 20 psi (138 kPa);    P<sub>peak hour</sub> ≥ 35 psi (240 kPa)
formulas.alt: Total distribution storage = Equalization Volume + Fire Suppression Reserve + Emergency Outage Reserve.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.6 & Ten States Standards: Water Distribution
formulas.notes: 20 psi absolute minimum under fire flow prevents back-siphonage of contaminated groundwater through joints.

formulas.name: Activated Sludge Food-to-Microorganism (F:M) Ratio
formulas.eq: F:M = Q · S0V · X = Q(MGD) × S0(mg/L) × 8.34V(MG) × MLVSS(mg/L) × 8.34 [day-1]
formulas.alt: Conventional aeration range: 0.2 - 0.5 lb BOD<sub>5</sub>/lb MLVSS · day; Extended aeration: 0.05 - 0.15 day<sup>-1</sup>.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.6: Wastewater - Activated Sludge
formulas.notes: Biomass X in the denominator must strictly be volatile suspended solids (MLVSS), not total suspended solids (MLSS).

formulas.name: Mean Cell Residence Time (MCRT / Sludge Age)
formulas.eq: θc = MCRT = Va Xa + Vc XcQw Xw + Qe Xe (days)
formulas.alt: Simplified (aeration solids only): θc = V XQw Xw + Qe Xe; Waste activated sludge pumping rate Qw = (V X / θc) - Qe XeXw.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.6: Wastewater - Solids Retention Time
formulas.notes: MCRT governs biological process selection: nitrification requires θ<sub>c</sub> ≥ 8 - 15 days in cold weather to retain slow-growing autotrophs.

formulas.name: Sanitary Gravity Sewer Minimum Self-Cleansing Slope
formulas.eq: Smin = [V · n1.486 Rh2/3]2 [for full pipe Rh = D/4]
formulas.alt: Ten States Standards: minimum slope achieves V ≥ 2.0 ft/s flowing full: 8-in = 0.40%, 10-in = 0.28%, 12-in = 0.22%, 15-in = 0.15%.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.6 & Ten States Standards: Wastewater Collection
formulas.notes: Minimum scouring velocity of 2.0 ft/s prevents deposition of putrescible organic fecal solids and hydrogen sulfide gas formation.

formulas.name: Lift Station Wet Well Minimum Cycle Time & Sizing
formulas.eq: Vactive = Tmin Qp4
formulas.alt: Cycle time: T = VQin + VQp - Qin; worst-case minimum cycle time occurs when influent inflow Qin = 0.5 Qp.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.6: Wastewater - Wet Well Design
formulas.notes: Protects submersible pump motors from overheating; typical pump manufacturers mandate T<sub>min</sub> ≥ 10 - 15 minutes (maximum 4-6 starts/hr).

formulas.name: Bacterial Monod Kinetics & Effluent Soluble Substrate
formulas.eq: μ = mumax SKs + S;    S = Ks(1 + b θc)θc(mumax - b) - 1
formulas.alt: Specific growth rate μ, half-velocity constant Ks, endogenous decay coefficient b, sludge age θc; Net yield: Yobs = Y1 + b θc.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.6: Wastewater - Biological Kinetics
formulas.notes: Shows that effluent soluble substrate concentration S is solely controlled by sludge age θ<sub>c</sub>, independent of influent concentration S<sub>0.</sub>

formulas.name: Anaerobic Digester Volatile Solids Reduction (Van Kleeck)
formulas.eq: VSR (%) = [VSin - VSoutVSin - (VSin · VSout) ight] × 100%
formulas.alt: Methane gas yield: CH<sub>4</sub> Volume (ft<sup>3</sup>/day) = 5.62 × (lb BOD<sub>L</sub> removed - 1.42 · P<sub>x</sub>); VS<sub>in</sub> and VS<sub>out</sub> expressed as decimals.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.6: Wastewater - Biosolids Digestion
formulas.notes: Van Kleeck equation accounts for the continuous reduction in total solid mass during biological volatile solids destruction.

formulas.name: Average End Area & Prismoidal Earthwork Volume
formulas.eq: VAEA = L (A1 + A22 × 27) (yd3);    Cp = L(c1 - c2)(w1 - w2)12 × 27;    Vp = VAEA - Cp
formulas.alt: Prismoidal formula: Vp = L(A1 + 4Am + A2)6 × 27; Borrow pit unit area method: V = Agrid4 × 27 [∑ h1 + 2∑ h2 + 3∑ h3 + 4∑ h4].
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 1.2: Construction - Earthwork
formulas.notes: Average End Area method consistently overestimates volume on tapering cuts/fills; prismoidal correction C<sub>p</sub> is subtracted to yield exact volume.

formulas.name: OSHA Excavation Safety Maximum Allowable Slopes
formulas.eq: Type A = 34H:1V (53°);    Type B = 1H:1V (45°);    Type C = 112H:1V (34°)
formulas.alt: Type A unconfined compressive strength q<sub>u</sub> ≥ 1.5 tsf; Type B: 0.5 < q<sub>u</sub> < 1.5 tsf; Type C: q<sub>u</sub> ≤ 0.5 tsf or submerged/granular.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 1.2 & OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart P: Safety
formulas.notes: Benching is strictly PROHIBITED in Type C soil. Trench excavations ≥ 5 ft deep require protective shoring/shields; spoils setback ≥ 2 ft.

formulas.name: Horizontal Circular Curve Geometry
formulas.eq: T = R tan(Δ2);    L = π R Δ180°;    E = R[1cos(Δ / 2) - 1];    M = R(1 - cosΔ2)
formulas.alt: Stationing: Station PT = Station PC + L; Middle ordinate sight clearance: Ms = R[1 - cos(28.65 SR)].
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 2.1: Geometric Design - Horizontal Curves
formulas.notes: Centerline route stationing runs along the curved arc length L from PC to PT, NEVER along tangent legs through PI.

formulas.name: Equal-Tangent Parabolic Vertical Curve Geometry
formulas.eq: y = ElevVPC + g1 x + (g2 - g12L) x2;    xturn = -g1 Lg2 - g1
formulas.alt: Elevation rate of change r = g2 - g1L = AL; Turning point (crest peak or sag low point) occurs where slope dydx = 0.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 2.2: Geometric Design - Vertical Curves
formulas.notes: Grade g<sub>1</sub>, g<sub>2</sub> entered in decimal or percent (with appropriate divisor); low point on sag curves dictates exact catch basin inlet placement.

formulas.name: Vertical Curve Sight Distance & K-Factor Design
formulas.eq: K = LA;    Lcrest = A S22,158 [for S ≤ L];    Lsag = A S2400 + 3.5 S [headlight S ≤ L]
formulas.alt: K-value represents horizontal distance (feet) required to achieve a 1% change in roadway gradient; A = |g<sub>2</sub> - g<sub>1</sub>|.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 2.2: Geometric Design - Vertical Sight Distance
formulas.notes: Crest curves governed by eye height (3.5 ft) and object height (2.0 ft); Sag curves governed by headlight beam angle (1° upward divergence).

formulas.name: Closed Traverse Compass (Bowditch) Balancing Rule
formulas.eq: Corrlat = -Δ Ltotal (li∑ l);    Corrdep = -Δ Dtotal (li∑ l)
formulas.alt: Linear misclosure = √(Δ Ltotal)2 + (Δ Dtotal)2; Precision = Linear MisclosureTraverse Perimeter.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 2.1: Surveying - Traverse Adjustment
formulas.notes: Distributes closure errors in latitude and departure proportionally to the length of each survey course; assumes equal measurement precision.

formulas.name: Retaining Wall Overturning & Sliding Stability
formulas.eq: FSoverturning = ∑ Mresist∑ Moverturn;    FSsliding = V tandelta + ca BH
formulas.alt: Moments taken about front toe; interface friction delta = 23φ'; Location of resultant: x = ∑ MnetV; Eccentricity e = B2 - x ≤ B6.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 3.4: Geotechnical - Retaining Wall Stability
formulas.notes: Design standards require FS<sub>overturning</sub> ≥ 2.0 and FS<sub>sliding</sub> ≥ 1.5; Resultant within middle-third (e ≤ B/6) avoids base tension.

formulas.name: Earthwork Volume Conversions (Bank, Loose, Compacted)
formulas.eq: VBCY = VCCY1 - Shrinkage;    VLCY = VBCY × (1 + Swell)
formulas.alt: Haul Truck Loads = VLCYTruck Capacity (LCY);    Excavator BCY/hr = LCY/hr1 + Swell
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 1.2: Construction Earthwork
formulas.notes: Bank Cubic Yards (BCY) is the in-situ reference state; always convert Compacted Fill (CCY) to BCY first before applying swell to get Loose Volume (LCY).

formulas.name: Cost Indexing, Power Sizing & Schedule Crashing Slope
formulas.eq: C2 = C1 (I2I1);    C2 = C1 (Q2Q1)m;    Cost Slope = Ccrash - Cnormaltnormal - tcrash
formulas.alt: Straight-Line Depreciation: D = C0 - Snn;    Book Value BVt = C0 - t · D
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 1.2 & 1.3: Cost Estimating & Depreciation
formulas.notes: Economies-of-scale exponent m is typically 0.6 to 0.7 for water/wastewater treatment tanks. Crash critical path activities starting with the lowest cost slope.

formulas.name: Darcy Constant-Head & Falling-Head Soil Permeameters
formulas.eq: kconst = Q · LA · h · t;    kfalling = a · LA · t ln(h1h2)
formulas.alt: Hazen empirical sand permeability: k (cm/s) ≈ C · (D<sub>10</sub>)<sup>2</sup> with D<sub>10</sub> in mm
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 3.1: Geotechnical - Permeability
formulas.notes: Constant-head test is used for clean sands and gravels; falling-head test with standpipe area a is used for fine silts and clays.

formulas.name: Infinite Slope Stability & Undrained Clay Strength
formulas.eq: FSseepage = (γ'gammasat) tanφ'tanβ;    FSdry = tanφ'tanβ;    cu = qu2
formulas.alt: Taylor cohesive slope stability: FS = cuNs · γ · H;    Triaxial failure: sinφ' = σ1 - σ3σ1 + σ3
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 3.1 & 3.5: Shear Strength & Slope Stability
formulas.notes: Parallel seepage to the ground surface cuts cohesionless slope factor of safety roughly in half (since γ' / gamma<sub>sat</sub> ≈ 0.5).

formulas.name: Zero Air Voids (ZAV) Curve & Relative Density of Sand
formulas.eq: gammaZAV = Gs γw1 + w Gs;    Dr (%) = [emax - eemax - emin] × 100%
formulas.alt: Relative Compaction: RC (%) = gammad,fieldgammad,max (Proctor) × 100%
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 3.1: Geotechnical - Compaction
formulas.notes: The Zero Air Voids curve corresponds to 100% saturation (S = 1.0) and represents the theoretical upper limit of any compaction curve.

formulas.name: AASHTO Group Index & Aggregate Moisture Absorption
formulas.alt: Aggregate Absorption (%) = (WSSD - WdryWdry) × 100%
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 1.5 & 3.1: Aggregates & AASHTO Classification
formulas.notes: AASHTO Group Index GI is rounded to the nearest whole non-negative integer; lower GI indicates superior pavement subgrade quality.

formulas.name: Parshall Flume, Broad-Crested Weir & Orifice Flow
formulas.eq: QParshall = 4.0 W Ha1.522W0.026;    Qbroad = 3.09 Cd b H1.5;    Qorifice = Cd Ao √2gh
formulas.alt: Venturi meter: Q = Cd A2 √2g Δ H1 - (D2/D1)4;    Δ Hwater = Δ hman (SGHg - 1)
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.1 & 4.2: Flow Measurement
formulas.notes: Sharp-edged circular orifice coefficient is typically C<sub>d</sub> ≈ 0.60 - 0.62; Venturi meter coefficient is C<sub>d</sub> ≈ 0.98.

formulas.name: Stokes Discrete Particle Settling & Clarifier Weir Loading
formulas.eq: vs = g(ρs - ρ) d218 μ = g(Gs - 1) d218 ν;    WLR = Qπ D [gpd/ft]
formulas.alt: Sludge Volume Index: SVI (mL/g) = SV30 (mL/L) × 1,000MLSS (mg/L)
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.6: Sedimentation & Activated Sludge
formulas.notes: Stokes law applies in the laminar settling regime (Reynolds number Re = v<sub>s</sub> d / ν < 0.5). Fractional removal for v<sub>s</sub> < SOR is R = v<sub>s</sub> / SOR.

formulas.name: Pipeline Thrust Block Force & Hardy Cross Loop Correction
formulas.eq: FT = 2 P A sin(θ2);    Δ Q = -∑ hf∑ |n · r · Qn-1|
formulas.alt: Equivalent Minor Loss Length: Leq = K · Df;    Sudden Enlargement: hL = (V1 - V2)22g
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.1: Pipe Networks & Thrust Restraint
formulas.notes: For a 90° pipe bend, sin(45°) = 0.7071 so resultant thrust is F<sub>T</sub> = 1.414 P A. Ensure pressure P (ψ) and area A (in<sup>2</sup>) have matching units.

formulas.name: Best Hydraulic Cross-Section & Horton Composite Roughness
formulas.eq: brect = 2y (Rh = y2);    ztrap = 1√3 = 0.577 (60° hexagon);    nc = [∑ (Pi ni1.5)Ptotal]2/3
formulas.alt: Specific Energy: E = y + V22g;    Specific Force: M = Q2g A + y A
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.2: Open Channel Hydraulics
formulas.notes: Best hydraulic section minimizes wetted perimeter P for a fixed flow area A, maximizing conveyance Q.

formulas.name: Channel Step Choke Transition & Riprap Stone Stability
formulas.eq: Δ zmax = E1 - Emin = E1 - 1.5 yc;    d50 = [VC √2g(Ss - 1)]2
formulas.alt: Strickler gravel roughness: n = 0.0395 (d<sub>50</sub>)<sup>1/6</sup> with d<sub>50</sub> in ft
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.2: Channel Transitions & Riprap
formulas.notes: If an upward floor step exceeds Δ z<sub>max</sub>, the flow chokes to critical depth over the step and backs up upstream water depth.

formulas.name: Horton & Green-Ampt Soil Infiltration Equations
formulas.eq: f(t) = fc + (f0 - fc)e-kt;    fGA(t) = K(1 + ψ ΔθF(t))
formulas.alt: Cumulative Horton Infiltration: F(t) = fc t + f0 - fck(1 - e-kt)
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.3: Hydrology - Infiltration
formulas.notes: As soil saturates over time (t → ∞ or F → ∞), infiltration capacity f(t) asymptotically approaches saturated conductivity f<sub>c</sub> or K.

formulas.name: Weibull Plotting Position, Normal Ratio & Lake Evaporation
formulas.eq: T = n + 1m;    p = mn + 1;    PX = NX3(PANA + PBNB + PCNC)
formulas.alt: Lake Evaporation: Elake = Kpan × Epan;    Bioretention Area: Af = WQv · dfk(hp + df)tf
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.3: Statistical Hydrology & Evaporation
formulas.notes: In Weibull frequency ranking, m = 1 is the largest flood in n years of record. Normal ratio method weights rain gauges by annual normals N<sub>i.</sub>

formulas.name: Well Specific Capacity, Well Efficiency & Capture Zone Width
formulas.eq: Specific Capacity = Qsw;    etawell = (sformationstotal) × 100%;    Wmax = QK b i
formulas.alt: Capture Zone Stagnation Point: xs = Q2π K b i;    Width at Well: Wwell = Wmax2
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.4: Well Performance & Capture Zones
formulas.notes: Total drawdown inside a pumped well casing equals laminar aquifer formation loss (B Q) plus turbulent screen/skin well loss (C Q<sup>2</sup>).

formulas.name: Unconfined Specific Yield, Theis Recovery & Sichardt Radius
formulas.eq: n = Sy + Sr;    s' = 2.303 Q4π Tlog10(tp + t't');    R0 = 3,000 sw √K
formulas.alt: AWWA A100 maximum well screen entrance velocity: v<sub>screen</sub> ≤ 0.1 ft/s
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.4: Aquifer Storage & Recovery Tests
formulas.notes: Specific yield S<sub>y</sub> is the gravity-drainable porosity of an unconfined aquifer. In Sichardt's formula, R<sub>0</sub> and s<sub>w</sub> are in meters and K is in m/s.

formulas.name: Henry's Law Gas Partitioning, First-Order Half-Life & Solubility
formulas.eq: Cair = H' · Cwater;    t1/2 = ln(2)k = 0.693k;    Ksp = [M2+][OH-]2
formulas.alt: First-order plug flow decay: C(t) = C0 e-kt where travel time t = DistanceVelocity
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.5: Environmental Chemistry & Kinetics
formulas.notes: Each 1.0 unit increase in pH increases [OH<sup>−</sup>] by 10×, reducing divalent metal solubility [M<sup>2+</sup>] by 100×.

formulas.name: O'Connor-Dobbins Reaeration, Vollenweider Lake P & Alkalinity
formulas.eq: kr = (Dm U)0.5H1.5;    Lc = [P]crit (zτw)(1 + √τw);    1.0 meq/L = 50 mg/L as CaCO3
formulas.alt: Total Suspended Solids: TSS (mg/L) = (Wdry - Wtare) (mg)Vsample (L)
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.5: Limnology & Water Quality
formulas.notes: Dissolved oxygen saturation DO<sub>sat</sub> decreases as water temperature increases or as elevation increases (lower atmospheric pressure).

formulas.name: Packed Tower Air Stripping, GAC EBCT & UV Fluence
formulas.eq: R = H'(GL);    NTU = (RR-1)ln[(Cin/Cout)(R-1)+1R];    EBCT = VmediaQ
formulas.alt: UV Disinfection Dose (Fluence): D (mJ/cm<sup>2</sup>) = I<sub>avg</sub> (mW/cm<sup>2</sup>) × t (s)
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.6.2 & 4.6.3: Adsorption, Stripping & UV
formulas.notes: Stripping factor R must exceed 1.0 for effective VOC removal; packing height is Z = HTU × NTU.

formulas.name: Langelier Saturation Index (LSI), Stage 2 DBP LRAA & Chemical Feed
formulas.eq: LSI = pH - pHs;    LRAA = Q1 + Q2 + Q3 + Q44 ≤ MCL;    Feed (gpd) = QMGD · Dose · 8.34SG · 8.34 · Purity
formulas.alt: LSI < 0: water is undersaturated and corrosive; LSI > 0: water is supersaturated and scale-forming.
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.5.1 & 4.6.2: Corrosion Control & Chemical Dosing
formulas.notes: Stage 2 DBP rule sets MCLs at 80 µg/L for TTHM and 60 µg/L for HAA5 based on the 4-quarter Locational Running Annual Average.

formulas.name: Harmon Sewer Peaking Factor, Kirschmer Bar Screen & Trickling Filter
formulas.eq: M = 1 + 144 + √P;    hL = β(wb)4/3(V22g)sinθ;    E1 = 1001 + 0.0561√WV · F
formulas.alt: Trickling Filter Recirculation Factor: F = 1 + R[1 + 0.1 R]2 where R = QrQ
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.6.4: Collection, Preliminary & Attached Growth
formulas.notes: In Harmon's formula, population P is entered in thousands. In the NRC trickling filter equation, W is in lb BOD5/day and V is in acre-ft.

formulas.name: Aeration Blower Sizing (SCFM), Nitrification & Sludge Thickening
formulas.eq: AOR = Q(S0 - S)8.34 - 1.42 Px + 4.57 Q(ΔNH4-N)8.34;    SCFM = SOTR1,440 × SOTE × 0.0174
formulas.alt: Sludge Thickening Volume Conservation: V<sub>1</sub> · S<sub>1</sub> = V<sub>2</sub> · S<sub>2</sub>;    Alkalinity Consumed = 7.14 × (ΔNH<sub>4-N</sub>)
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.6.4: Aeration, BNR & Biosolids
formulas.notes: Nitrification requires 4.57 lb O<sub>2</sub> and consumes 7.14 lb CaCO<sub>3</sub> alkalinity per lb of ammonia-N oxidized to nitrate.

formulas.name: Limit of Economic Haul, Equipment Productivity & Trench Dewatering
formulas.eq: LEH = FHD + (CborrowCoverhaul) × 100 ft;    CCY/hr = 16.3 · Weff · Smph · Lin · EffP
formulas.alt: Trench Dewatering (2-sided unconfined): Qtotal = 2 · L · K(H2 - hw2)2 R0;    Curvature & Refraction: hcr = 0.0206 M2
formulas.ref: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 1.2, 2.1 & 4.4: Sitework, Surveying & Dewatering
formulas.notes: When haul distance exceeds LEH, it is more economical to waste excavated cut and borrow from an off-site pit.

Project Planning.overview: Covers engineering economics (Present Worth, Annual Equivalent, B/C Ratio, Capitalized Cost), Critical Path Method (CPM) network scheduling & crashing, and earthwork swell/shrinkage quantity takeoffs.
setupSteps: Step 1 — Draw the Cash-Flow or Network Diagram: For economics, map Year 0 capital cost (P), recurring annual O&M (A), and terminal salvage value (F) over common analysis horizon n. For scheduling, trace all network paths from Start to Finish.
Step 2 — Convert Soil States via Bank Volume (BCY): Always use undisturbed Bank Cubic Yards (BCY) as your pivot: VBCY = VCCY1 − Shrinkage and VLCY = VBCY × (1 + Swell).
Step 3 — Select the Exact Factor Formula: Use (P/A, i, n) to bring annual O&M to Present Worth, or (A/P, i, n) to annualize upfront capital investment for EUAC and B/C ratios.
Step 4 — Check Salvage Signs & Float Rules: Salvage value is a positive cash inflow (reduces net cost). On CPM networks, Critical Path has Total Float TF = LS − ES = 0.
Project Planning.unitTraps: Never add undiscounted annual O&M directly to initial capital cost. When crashing schedules, always crash the critical path activity with the lowest cost slope ($/day) first.

Soil Mechanics.overview: Covers 3-phase soil weight-volume relationships, effective stress with groundwater, Darcy permeability tests, Terzaghi consolidation settlement & time rate, Rankine lateral earth pressures, and bearing capacity.
setupSteps: Step 1 — Anchor Phase Relations with S·e = w·Gs: In saturated soils (S = 1.0), void ratio is immediately e = w·Gs. Always compute dry unit weight γd = γtotal1 + w first when given wet weight and moisture content.

Step 2 — Separate Total Stress, Pore Pressure, and Effective Stress: Compute total overburden stress σ = ∑(γi·zi) from ground surface down, subtract hydrostatic pore pressure u = γw·zw below the water table, and get σ′ = σ − u.
Step 3 — Check Drainage Path Hdr in Consolidation: For double-drained clay layers (sand above and below), Hdr = H2. For single-drained clay (impermeable rock boundary), Hdr = H.

Step 4 — Distinguish Active, Passive, and At-Rest Walls: Yielding retaining walls use Rankine Ka = tan2(45° − φ′2); rigid basement walls use Jaky at-rest K0 = 1 − sin φ′. Water pressure ALWAYS acts with K = 1.0!
Soil Mechanics.unitTraps: In USCS units, γ<sub>w</sub> = 62.4 lb/ft<sup>3</sup>. Primary consolidation settlement uses base-10 logarithm (log<sub>10</sub>), whereas falling-head permeability uses natural log (ln).

Materials.handbookRef: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Sections 1.5 (Construction Materials) & 3.1 (Soil Classification)
Materials.overview: Covers USCS and AASHTO soil classification (Casagrande plasticity chart A-line, Cu and Cc), Portland cement concrete mix design (w/c ratio, batch yield, slump, air entrainment), and pressure pipe ratings (PVC, HDPE, DIP, RCP).
setupSteps: Step 1 — Check #200 Sieve (0.075 mm) First for Soil Classification: If > 50% passes #200, it is fine-grained (use Liquid Limit LL and Plasticity Index PI = LL − PL against the A-Line PIA = 0.73(LL − 20)). If < 50% passes #200, it is coarse-grained (check #4 sieve for Gravel vs. Sand, then evaluate Cu and Cc).

Step 2 — Base Concrete Mix Adjustments on SSD Aggregate State: Free surface moisture above Saturated Surface-Dry (SSD) adds water to the batch; aggregate absorption below SSD subtracts water from the batch.
Step 3 — Use Dimension Ratio (DR) for Thermoplastic Pipes: For AWWA C900 PVC and PE4710 HDPE pipe, working pressure rating is PR = 2·HDSDR − 1, where DR = Dot.
Step 4 — Convert RCP D-Load to Field Trench Strength: Required 3-edge bearing strength TEB = WfieldBf, and D-Load = TEBDinside (ft).
Materials.unitTraps: Water weighs 8.34 lb/gal (62.4 lb/ft<sup>3</sup>). 1 cubic yard of concrete = 27 ft<sup>3</sup>. Do NOT include the #200 sieve when summing cumulative percent retained for Fineness Modulus (FM).

Analysis and Design.handbookRef: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.5 & 4.6 (Hydraulic & Process Analysis)
Analysis and Design.overview: Covers conservative and 1st-order non-conservative river mixing mass balances, clarifier Surface Overflow Rate (SOR), Solids Loading Rate (SLR), Weir Loading Rate (WLR), weirs, flumes, Venturi/orifice meters, Stokes settling, and Camp velocity gradient (G).
setupSteps: Step 1 — Draw a Control Volume for Mass Balances: At any stream mixing junction, downstream flow is Qdown = Qstream + Qeff, and mixed concentration is Cmix = QstreamCstream + QeffCeffQstream + Qeff.

Step 2 — Separate Primary vs. Secondary Clarifier Flows: Primary clarifier Surface Overflow Rate SOR = QAplan uses forward flow Q only (depth does not affect SOR). Secondary clarifier Solids Loading Rate SLR MUST include Return Activated Sludge flow: Solids = (Q + QRAS) × MLSS × 8.34.
Step 3 — Match Weir & Flume Exponents: Rectangular suppressed/contracted weirs scale with H1.5 (Q = 3.33·L·H1.5), whereas 90° V-notch weirs scale with H2.5 (Q = 2.50·H2.5).
Step 4 — Convert Power to ft·lb/s for Mixing Gradient G: In USCS units, multiply horsepower by 550 ft·lb/(s·hp) before plugging into G = √Pμ·V.
Analysis and Design.unitTraps: Always remember the 'Pound Formula': Mass (lb/day) = Flow (MGD) × Concentration (mg/L) × 8.34. And 1 MGD = 1.547 cfs = 694.4 gpm.

Hydraulics-Closed Conduit.handbookRef: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.1 (Closed Conduit Hydraulics & Pumps)
Hydraulics-Closed Conduit.overview: Covers Energy & Hydraulic Grade Lines (EGL/HGL), Darcy-Weisbach & Hazen-Williams friction losses, series/parallel pipe networks, pump Total Dynamic Head (TDH), Brake & Wire-to-Water Horsepower, Pump Affinity Laws, NPSHa cavitation, water hammer surges, and pipe thrust blocks.
setupSteps: Step 1 — Write the Extended Bernoulli Energy Equation from Suction to Discharge: z1 + P1γ + V122g + TDH = z2 + P2γ + V222g + hf + hm.
Step 2 — Check Pipe Units in Hazen-Williams: If flow Q is in cfs and diameter D is in feet, use hf = 4.73·L·Q1.852C1.852·D4.87. If Q is in gpm and d is in inches, use constant 10.44.
Step 3 — Track Pump Efficiency Stages: Water Horsepower WHP = Q (gpm) × TDH (ft) × SG3,960. Divide by ηpump for Brake HP, and divide by (ηpump × ηmotor) for electrical Wire-to-Water HP.
Step 4 — Check Suction Lift Sign in NPSHa: NPSHa = Hbarometric ± zstatic − hf,suction − Hvapor. Subtract zstatic when the pump is located ABOVE the suction reservoir water surface!
Hydraulics-Closed Conduit.unitTraps: 1 psi = 2.31 ft of water (at SG = 1.0). In thrust block calculations, FT = 2·P·A·sin(θ2) requires pressure P in psi and pipe area A in in2 (or psf and ft2).

Hydraulics-Open Channel.handbookRef: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.2 (Open Channel Hydraulics)
Hydraulics-Open Channel.overview: Covers Manning's uniform flow equation, normal depth, specific energy, critical depth, Froude number regimes, hydraulic jumps & energy dissipation, circular sewer partial-flow elements, gradually varied flow profiles (M1, M2, S1), culverts, and HEC-22 street gutter spread.
setupSteps: Step 1 — Compute Geometric Elements First: For a trapezoid with bottom width b and side slope z (zH:1V), Area A = (b + z·y)y, Wetted Perimeter P = b + 2y√1 + z2, Top Width T = b + 2z·y, and Hydraulic Radius Rh = AP.
Step 2 — Check Flow Regime with Froude Number: Fr = V√g·Dh where hydraulic depth Dh = AT. Fr < 1 is Subcritical (downstream control); Fr = 1 is Critical; Fr > 1 is Supercritical (upstream control).

Step 3 — Distinguish Alternate Depths vs. Conjugate (Sequent) Depths: Alternate depths share the same Specific Energy E = y + V22g (smooth transition). Conjugate depths across a Hydraulic Jump share the same Specific Force (momentum) and follow y2y1 = 12(√1 + 8Fr12 − 1).
Step 4 — Use Partial-Flow Ratios for Circular Conduits: A half-full circular pipe (dD = 0.50) has A = 12Afull and Rh = D4 (same Rh and velocity as a full pipe!).
Hydraulics-Open Channel.unitTraps: In USCS units, Manning's equation MUST include the 1.486 factor: Q = 1.486nA·Rh2/3S1/2. The relation yc = (q2g)1/3 and Emin = 1.5yc applies ONLY to rectangular channels!

Hydrology.overview: Covers Rational Method peak runoff, IDF curves, Time of Concentration (NRCS sheet flow & Kirpich), NRCS (SCS) Curve Number runoff depth & volume, Unit Hydrographs, Muskingum flood routing, Horton/Green-Ampt infiltration, flood return period binomial risk, and Water Quality Volume (WQv).
setupSteps: Step 1 — Match Storm Duration to Time of Concentration (tc): In the Rational Method (Q = Cf·C·I·A), sum all travel times along the longest hydraulic path to find tc, then read rainfall intensity I from the IDF curve at duration td = tc.

Step 2 — Partition Rainfall in the NRCS Curve Number Method: First compute maximum soil retention S = 1,000CN − 10 (inches). Check that rainfall P > 0.2S, then compute direct runoff depth Q = (P − 0.2S)2P + 0.8S (inches).

Step 3 — Convert Runoff Depth (inches) to Volume (acre-ft or ft3): Multiply runoff depth Q (in inches) by watershed area A (in acres) and divide by 12 in/ft to get Volume in acre-feet (1 acre = 43,560 ft2).
Step 4 — Use Binomial Probability for Multi-Year Flood Risk: Annual exceedance probability is p = 1T. The probability that a T-year flood occurs at least once in n years is Risk = 1 − (1 − 1T)n.
Hydrology.unitTraps: In Kirpich's tc equation and HEC-22 gutter equations, enter slope S in ft/ft (decimal), NOT percent. In the Schueler WQv equation (Rv = 0.05 + 0.009·I), enter imperviousness I as a whole percentage (e.g., 60 for 60%).

Groundwater and Wells.handbookRef: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.4 (Groundwater & Well Hydraulics)
Groundwater and Wells.overview: Covers Darcy's law & actual pore seepage velocity, aquifer transmissivity & storativity, Thiem steady confined radial flow, Dupuit steady unconfined radial flow, Theis & Cooper-Jacob transient well drawdown, well interference superposition, 2D seepage flow nets, and Ghyben-Herzberg saltwater intrusion.
setupSteps: Step 1 — Distinguish Darcy Velocity vs. Actual Seepage Velocity: Darcy discharge velocity v = QA = K·i is a superficial velocity across the gross area. True pore seepage velocity for contaminant travel time is vs = K·ine.

Step 2 — Identify Confined (Thiem) vs. Unconfined (Dupuit) Well Hydraulics: Confined aquifers have constant thickness b (transmissivity T = K·b) and use linear drawdown difference (s1 − s2). Unconfined aquifers have a sloping water table and use the difference of SQUARED saturated heads (h22 − h12).

Step 3 — Superpose Drawdowns Linearly for Multiple Wells: In confined aquifers, total drawdown at any observation point from multiple pumping wells is the algebraic sum of individual drawdowns: stotal = sA + sB.
Step 4 — Check Flow Net Shape Factor (NfNd): Seepage under a dam per unit width is q = K·H·(NfNd), where H is net head difference between upstream and downstream pools.
Groundwater and Wells.unitTraps: 1 ft3 = 7.4805 gallons, and 1 day = 1,440 minutes (so 1 gpm = 192.5 ft3/day). Always pair observation well radii properly: closer well r1 has larger drawdown s1, but smaller saturated thickness h1.

Surface Water & Groundwater Quality.handbookRef: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.5 (Environmental & Water Quality)
Surface Water & Groundwater Quality.overview: Covers Streeter-Phelps dissolved oxygen sag curves, critical time & critical DO deficit, BOD5 vs. Ultimate BOD kinetics, Arrhenius temperature corrections, nitrogenous oxygen demand (NBOD), Clean Water Act TMDLs, Henry's law partitioning, and groundwater contaminant retardation.
setupSteps: Step 1 — Mix River & Effluent Conditions at x = 0 First: Before applying Streeter-Phelps, compute the mixed initial ultimate BOD (L0) and mixed initial DO deficit (D0 = DOsat − DOmix) immediately downstream of the outfall.
Step 2 — Convert BOD5 to Ultimate BODu (L0): Streeter-Phelps requires Ultimate BOD! Convert 5-day BOD using L0 = BOD51 − e−5k.
Step 3 — Adjust Rate Constants for Stream Temperature: Use kT = k20·θT − 20, with θ = 1.047 for biological deoxygenation (kd) and θ = 1.024 for atmospheric reaeration (kr).
Step 4 — Account for Soil Sorption Retardation in Aquifers: Retardation factor Rd = 1 + (ρbn)Kd slows down the dissolved contaminant plume: vplume = vseepageRd.
Surface Water & Groundwater Quality.unitTraps: Check whether BOD rate constant k is given in base e or base 10 (kbase e = 2.303 × Kbase 10). Remember that Minimum River DO = DOsat − Dc.

Drinking Water Distribution & Treatment.handbookRef: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Sections 4.6.1–4.6.3 (Water Treatment & Distribution)
Drinking Water Distribution & Treatment.overview: Covers chemical dosing & metering pumps, alum coagulation alkalinity consumption, lime-soda ash softening (CH vs. NCH), rapid/flocculant/granular filtration & backwashing, membrane filtration (UF/RO) mass balances, disinfection CT compliance & baffling factors, GAC adsorption, air stripping, LSI corrosion, and distribution storage.
setupSteps: Step 1 — Account for Solution Purity & Specific Gravity in Liquid Chemical Feeds: Active dry chemical mass (lb/day) = Q (MGD) × Dose (mg/L) × 8.34. Divide by (SG × 8.34 lb/gal × Purity fraction) to get liquid metering pump rate in gal/day.

Step 2 — Partition Carbonate vs. Non-Carbonate Hardness (as CaCO3): If Total Hardness (TH) > Total Alkalinity (TA), then Carbonate Hardness CH = TA and Non-Carbonate Hardness NCH = TH − TA. If TH ≤ TA, then CH = TH and NCH = 0.
Step 3 — Use Effective Contact Time t10 for Disinfection CT: Never use theoretical detention time T = VQ directly in CT compliance; multiply by the baffling factor (BF = t10T) so that t10 = T × BF.
Step 4 — Sum All Three Components for Distribution Tank Storage: Total Tank Volume = Equalizing Volume + Fire Flow Volume (Qfire × Duration) + Emergency Reserve.
Drinking Water Distribution & Treatment.unitTraps: 1 meq/L of hardness or alkalinity = 50 mg/L as CaCO<sub>3</sub>. Equivalence weights as CaCO<sub>3</sub>: Ca<sup>2+</sup> = 20.0, Mg<sup>2+</sup> = 12.2, Na<sup>+</sup> = 23.0, HCO<sub>3</sub><sup>−</sup> = 61.0.

Wastewater Collection & Treatment.handbookRef: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Section 4.6.4 (Wastewater Collection & Treatment)
Wastewater Collection & Treatment.overview: Covers sanitary sewer peaking factors (Harmon) & self-cleansing slopes, lift station wet well cycle sizing, grit chambers, primary clarifier sludge mass balance, activated sludge F:M ratio & MCRT (sludge age), Monod kinetics, aeration blower SCFM sizing, nitrification/denitrification stoichiometry, trickling filters (NRC), and anaerobic digestion (Van Kleeck).
setupSteps: Step 1 — Use Volatile Biomass (MLVSS) for Activated Sludge F:M Ratio: Food-to-Microorganism ratio F:M = Q · S0V · Xv divides daily influent BOD5 load by aeration basin volatile suspended solids (MLVSS).

Step 2 — Track All Solids Exiting the System for MCRT (Sludge Age): Mean Cell Residence Time θc = V · MLSSQw·Xw + Qe·Xe divides total system inventory by daily solids wasted PLUS solids lost in the plant effluent.

Step 3 — Include Both Carbonaceous and Nitrogenous Oxygen Demand in Aeration: Total oxygen required = Carbonaceous oxygen demand − 1.42(Biomass wasted) + 4.57(Ammonia-N oxidized). Nitrification also consumes 7.14 mg CaCO3 alkalinity per mg NH4-N oxidized.

Step 4 — Conserve Dry Solids Mass Across Sludge Thickeners & Dewatering: Since dry solids mass is conserved (assuming 100% capture), wet sludge volume varies inversely with percent solids: V1 · (% Solids1) = V2 · (% Solids2).
Wastewater Collection & Treatment.unitTraps: In the NRC trickling filter formula, organic loading W is in lb/day and media volume V MUST be in acre-feet (divide ft3 by 43,560). Standard air contains 0.0174 lb O2 per SCFM.

Project Sitework.handbookRef: NCEES Handbook v2.2, Sections 1.2 (Earthwork & OSHA Safety), 2.1 (Horizontal Curves & Surveying) & 2.2 (Vertical Curves)
Project Sitework.overview: Covers Average End Area & Prismoidal earthwork volumes, borrow pit grid volumes, mass haul Limit of Economic Haul, OSHA Subpart P excavation slopes & trench shoring pressures, horizontal circular & compound curves, vertical crest/sag curves & sight distance, and survey traverse balancing (Bowditch rule).
setupSteps: Step 1 — Advance Route Stationing Along the Curve Arc (Never Through PI): On horizontal circular curves, Point of Tangency is Sta PT = Sta PC + L (where arc length L = π·R·Δ180°), whereas on parabolic vertical curves, stationing is measured horizontally (1 station = 100 ft).

Step 2 — Locate Vertical Curve Turning Points Relative to VPC: Distance from VPC to the crest high point or sag low point is xturn = −g1·Lg2 − g1. Then plug xturn into the parabola elevation equation.

Step 3 — Apply OSHA 29 CFR 1926 Subpart P Trench Rules: Maximum allowable excavation slopes (<20 ft deep): Type A = 34H:1V (53°); Type B = 1H:1V (45°); Type C = 112H:1V (34°). Trenches ≥ 4 ft deep require ladder egress within 25 ft lateral travel; trenches ≥ 5 ft deep require shoring/shielding.

Step 4 — Weight Borrow Pit Grid Corners by Shared Cells: Multiply corner depths by the number of grid squares touching that stake (1 for exterior corners, 2 for side edges, 3 for reflex corners, 4 for interior stakes): V = Agrid4 × 27(∑h1 + 2∑h2 + 3∑h3 + 4∑h4).
Project Sitework.unitTraps: Always divide cubic feet (ft<sup>3</sup>) by 27 to get cubic yards (yd<sup>3</sup>). In Bowditch compass traverse adjustment, the correction sign is OPPOSITE to the total misclosure error.
